headline: Warmer weather dents revenue, but core earnings hold up
summary_short: MDU's Q1 2026 revenue fell 10.2% y/y to $606.0M on warmer weather and lower pass-through gas costs, while EBITDA rose 2.0% to $172.5M and net income slipped 1.4% to $80.8M ($0.39 diluted EPS) on higher interest expense.
summary_long: Consolidated earnings fell $1.2M (-1.4%) y/y to $80.8M as warmer weather cut retail electric and gas volumes; gas-distribution revenue fell $76.8M on lower pass-through commodity costs recovered dollar-for-dollar in rates, so the revenue drop carried no margin impact. Rate relief in Washington, Idaho, Montana and Wyoming partly offset the volume hit. Electric earnings dipped on higher interest expense and Badger Wind Farm depreciation despite higher renewable-tracker revenue; pipeline earnings fell on lower storage withdrawals and higher O&M. Operating cash flow dropped 31.4% to $149.2M on lower gas-cost and carbon-compliance collections. The company raised $81.2M via equity issuance, repaid $218.9M of debt, and built cash to $53.3M (+88.9% q/q). FY2026 capex guidance held at ~$565.4M.

drivers.explanation: Consolidated earnings fell $1.2M as weather-driven volume declines and higher interest expense across the electric, gas distribution and pipeline segments outweighed rate relief and an income-tax benefit in the Other segment.

Revenue fell mainly on $76.7M lower pass-through purchased-gas costs (warmer weather, lower volumes) recovered in customer rates, plus lower retail volumes, partly offset by $9.4M of rate relief in WA/ID/MT/WY.

EPS fell in step with the $1.2M net-income decline, diluted slightly further by ~1% more weighted-average shares outstanding following the December 2025 follow-on offering and March 2026 forward-sale settlement.

EBITDA rose despite lower revenue because purchased-gas cost pass-throughs fell in step with gas revenue, while electric and gas-distribution operating income both grew on rate relief and renewable-tracker recovery.

Electric operating income rose 16.6% on higher renewable-tracker revenue from Badger Wind Farm and recovered fuel costs; gas-distribution operating income rose 3.1% as lower revenue-based taxes offset volume declines.
The $68.3M y/y decline was largely due to $40.8M lower collections of purchased gas costs and $33.2M lower carbon-compliance cost collections, partly offset by higher receivables collections.
Cash capex was roughly flat y/y ($92.4M vs $93.0M); the MD&A separately cites $83.4M of accrual-basis capital spending for the quarter, up from $79.8M a year ago.
Cash built q/q mainly from $138.4M of new long-term debt issuance and $81.2M of net equity proceeds, partly offset by $218.9M of debt repayment and $91.2M of investing outflows.
Not explained as a standalone line in the release; the q/q decline is consistent with $218.9M of debt repayment during the quarter exceeding $138.4M of new long-term debt issuance.
Equity rose q/q mainly on $81.2M of net proceeds from a partial forward-sale-agreement settlement plus retained net income, partially offset by $28.6M of dividends paid.
